6. Physical initialization and destructive readout

Known-state preparation executes the finite fault-tolerant factories recursively from noisy native cup states and resets. There is no free supply of perfect encoded ancillas.

For destructive readout, fuse every bottom data carrier in the $Z$ basis. The ideal full-space instrument includes local leakage repair, while faults in the physical repair, fusion and recorded bit are counted.

A good measurement hierarchy is $(r,1)$-sparse. Combined with the computational deviation, its support is
$(r,32)+(r,1)\subseteq(r,33),$
within the actual classical correction radius $127$.

At each level, correct the measured word to a nearest $C_{\mathrm{cl}}$ word and then return its $C_{\mathrm{cl}}/D_{\mathrm{cl}}$ coset. Exhaustive fixed-code decoding is a valid implementation; its large constant work is charged.

On every good support, logical basis outcomes are exact. Positivity forces the restricted POVM to be the ideal logical-$Z$ POVM. Because quantum data are discarded, this also determines the complete classical/reference channel.

The classical decoder finishes after destructive measurement. Its latency does not create an uncharged quantum waiting period. Retained quantum outputs instead require continued protected identity work.


7. Local control and full polynomial costs

Select a dyadic
$\epsilon_0\le\min(\epsilon,1),$
within a factor four when $\epsilon\le1$. Let $B_\epsilon$ be the supplied rational’s bit length; its reading and storage costs are charged.

Use gate-choice-independent bounds
$n_0=S+1,\qquad
D_0=32(S+1)^2,\qquad
\overline N=128(S+1)^3.$
They cover serial logical routing, restoration of home order, logical idles, known-input endpoints and readout roots.

Choose
$H=\max\!\left\{2,
\left\lceil\log_2\frac{128\overline N}{\epsilon_0}\right\rceil
\right\},
\qquad
r=\lceil\log_2H\rceil.$
Then even the loose bound $4\overline Nq_r$ is below $\epsilon$.

The expanded quantum schedule satisfies
$W\le n_0b^r,\qquad
T\le \beta D_0\tau^r.$
In particular,
$b^r\le(2H)^{\log_2b},\qquad
\tau^r\le(2H)^{\log_2\tau}.$

Place the native quantum array in a constant-height strip. Above each controller place a vertical tape containing its $T$ instructions.
